summary: AE + SE met with Polaris Health team to scope a 6-week POC focused on inference cost and latency improvements for their clinical summarization and triage pipelines. Key success criteria discussed: p95 latency <= 350ms for short-chat flows, p95 <= 1s for 1k-token summaries; end-to-end throughput targets & 3x reduction in per-session inference cost versus current hosted provider; data controls (VPC, KMS) and SOC2 evidence required. Agreed timeline includes kickoff, access/setup, baseline benchmarks, mid-point optimization & tuning, and an executive readout. Next steps: share SOW and benchmark plan, customer to provide sample traffic and credentials to test environment.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jenna Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Polaris Head of ML), Tom Rivera (Polaris Platform Eng), Leah Chen (Polaris Security), Mike O'Neill (Polaris PM)

Summary (auto): quick scoping to align on success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, and a 6-week POC timeline with milestones.

00:00 Jenna Park: hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you making time, um quick intros then we can jump into the goals for the POC
00:12 Aisha Khan: hi all, aisha here, we run ML infra and models for triage and clinical summarization, we want to validate inference economics and get latency down for our in-app flows
00:25 Tom Rivera: tom - platform eng - I'll give access and help with traces and infra linking
00:34 Marcus Lee: cool, from Redwood I'll run the benchmark plan and help size the workload, we'll need sample traffic and a few test endpoints
00:48 Mike O'Neill: our timeline is tight, execs want a readout in early May so looking at about six weeks total, is that what you had in mind?
01:05 Jenna Park: yeah that's consistent. high-level we usually do kickoff, access/setup, baseline benchmark, mid-point review for tuning, then exec readout. for a six-week we do about two weeks for setup/baseline then two weeks of optimization then one final week for readout prep
01:35 Leah Chen: security first - we need SOC2 evidence, SSO/SAML integration, audit logs, and KMS/HSM encryption for keys. Also data residency - some PII must stay in our VPC
01:50 Marcus Lee: totally understood. Redwood Private or Dedicated options can satisfy that; for the POC we can either run in your VPC private deployment or a dedicated isolated pool, depends on what access you can give for the 2-4 week test. For quickness hosted with strict retention rules is possible but we know you said no clear text cloud logs, right?
02:12 Leah Chen: yeah hosted is trickier. we prefer VPC peering or a private deployment. for the POC we can allow a temporary VPC peered test env if you support KMS integration
02:28 Jenna Park: we do KMS integrations and will share the security package. we'll note action item to surface SOC2 docs and KMS flow to Leah.
02:42 Aisha Khan: success criteria - operationally we care about latency on the triage flow (short requests ~20-50 tokens) and summarization (avg 800-1200 tokens). target is p95 latency under 350ms for short flows and under 1s for the longer summaries; also cost per session must be lower than their current provider by at least 2x-3x
03:10 Marcus Lee: that's helpful. can you give rough traffic numbers? concurrency, QPS, avg tokens?
03:20 Tom Rivera: peak concurrency is about 120 concurrent requests for triage flows across regions, baseline average request size 40 tokens; summarization workload is lower QPS but heavier tokens - maybe 50 concurrent during batch windows and typical summarization is 900 tokens avg. daily volume is ~50k triage requests and 8k summaries
03:45 Marcus Lee: okay so for benchmarking we'll model two profiles: "short interactive" (40 tokens, p95 target 350ms) and "long summaries" (900 tokens, p95 target 1s). We'll run baseline against your current provider, then Redwood hosted and a dedicated config; will measure p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and cost per 1k tokens
04:05 Mike O'Neill: we also want model quality comparison - same prompt set and a small eval harness to check hallucination/regression
04:18 Marcus Lee: yes we'll include a fixed eval prompt set and automated scoring so we don't accidentally trade quality for cost. we'll include generation sampling seeds where possible
04:32 Jenna Park: timeline and milestones - propose kickoff 2026-04-02, access/setup week 1 (credentials, SSO, KMS, sample data), baseline benchmark week 2 (run baseline + record metrics), optimization weeks 3-4 (batching, quantization suggestions, model variants), mid-point review week 4 (metrics + tuning plan), final validation week 5, exec readout week 6 (2026-05-11 window). does that align?
05:00 Aisha Khan: yes that works. can we have an internal mid-point demo for the engineering execs too? maybe add 30-min slot after the mid-point review
05:12 Jenna Park: yes we can do a 30-min mid-point demo. we'll add to milestones.
05:22 Tom Rivera: about access - we'll provide three things: (1) anonymized sample traces, (2) a test VPC for peering with KMS, (3) a service account with limited scope. is that sufficient?
05:34 Marcus Lee: that's perfect. for the private peering we'll need network CIDRs and a couple firewall rules, and a small test dataset for the eval harness
05:48 Leah Chen: one more on compliance - we need to confirm data retention/ logs and the ability to turn off cloud-side KV cache persistence, and we want audit logs to be forwarded to our SIEM
06:05 Marcus Lee: we can configure cache TTLs and we have audit log forwarding; I'll include the specifics in the security package.
06:15 Mike O'Neill: on benchmarks - do you have a standard harness we can run in our environment or do you prefer Redwood-run tests?
06:25 Marcus Lee: both. we provide a load script and metric collectors that you can run in your environment to capture network hops. we can also run Redwood-hosted harness against the test endpoints to compare. ideally we do both to rule out network variance.
06:40 Jenna Park: ok let's go through acceptance criteria again for clarity
06:44 Aisha Khan: 1) p95 latency under 350ms (triage) and under 1s (summaries) against POC test load 2) cost per session at least 2x improvement vs current provider on comparable configs 3) no data leaving VPC or plain-text logs 4) exec signoff on quality regression test (automated eval)
07:10 Marcus Lee: noted. for cost targets we'll provide numbers in SOW - ballpark we expect 40-60% token cost reduction with batching + quantization for your workload, but real numbers will come from baseline runs
07:28 Tom Rivera: about model variants - do you recommend a single model or an ensemble for the POC?
07:33 Marcus Lee: for scoping we usually start with one model variant close to your current in quality, plus a trimmed quantized variant for cost tests. if latency is tight we try smaller causal models or tuned context window configurations. we'll include model catalog options in the SOW
07:50 Leah Chen: any legal checklist items we should be aware of to approve the POC?
07:57 Jenna Park: we'll share a short checklist - IP, data handling, access windows, and liability limits for the POC; full legal contracting to follow if POC goes well
08:10 Mike O'Neill: ok great. what does success look like at the mid-point?
08:16 Marcus Lee: at mid-point we want baseline metrics, first round of optimizations applied (e.g., batching, KV caching), and a measured delta in latency/cost. we'll demo the dashboard with per-route traces and token-level cost breakdowns
08:34 Aisha Khan: can you also capture memory/GPU utilization and model warmup behaviors? we had weird cold-starts with previous provider
08:42 Marcus Lee: yes we'll capture cold-starts and warm cache scenarios; we'll note warm-up sequences in test plan
09:02 Jenna Park: ok I'll recap milestones in the SOW: kickoff 4/2, access/setup week 1, baseline week 2, optimization weeks 3-4, mid-point review week 4, final validation week 5, exec readout week 6 (week of 5/11).
09:25 Tom Rivera: we can aim to provide traces and VPC peering info by 3/30.
09:32 Leah Chen: security will review SOC2 docs by 3/31 and confirm KMS requirements.
09:40 Jenna Park: perfect. any other questions or blockers?
09:44 Aisha Khan: just one - do you support integration with our internal monitoring (Datadog)? we'd like end-to-end traces linked to our APM
09:52 Marcus Lee: yes we have tracing hooks and can forward metrics to Datadog; we'll include the instrumentation steps in the plan
10:05 Mike O'Neill: great, thanks. looks like we have alignment. Jenna, you'll share the SOW and benchmark plan and Marcus will own the test harness and mid-point deliverables
10:14 Jenna Park: exactly. we'll send action items and calendar invites after this call. thanks everyone
10:20 (end of recorded transcript)
notes: References: SOW template link (shared in chat), Security package link to be shared by Jenna, Benchmark harness repo (private) to be provided by Marcus.
